transcript:
Header: 2026-01-18 15:00 UTC | Duration ~48m | Attendees: Evan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Mark (Copperfield CTO), Ana (ML Eng), Raj (PM)

[00:00] Evan: Hey everyone thanks for making time, quick intro — I'm Evan from Redwood Inference, this is Priya our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:12] Mark: Good, thanks. We're excited to see how the hosted endpoints could replace some of our current search infra.
[00:20] Raj: Yeah we want to reduce latency and cost, but keep relevance high — that's the tradeoff.
[00:30] Priya: Great, today we'll demo embeddings + rerank endpoints, show Console tuning, and Optimizes suggestions — then talk pilot. I'll demo live queries against a sanitized product corpus.
[01:10] (note: audio glitch at 01:04)
[02:05] Priya: Quick architecture slide — client -> hosted API (embeddings) -> vector index -> recall -> reranker endpoint (hosted) -> final ranking. We're using prefix caching and optional KV cache to store long context for conversational flows.
[03:00] Ana: Quick question: we currently use Pinecone for vectors and an internal BERT re-ranker on CPU. We're curious about latency for a full rerank call on hosted.
[03:18] Priya: Good Q. For the hosted reranker endpoint we typically see 60-120ms p50 for a 128-token rerank model on the 8xA100 backends with our batching config. It depends on model size, sequence length, and batch window. Those numbers can vary — but we have verified profiles in the Console.
[04:05] Mark: And cost? Our Ops lead will ask about per-req dollars.
[04:10] Evan: We gave rough ballparks in the deck — embeddings are cheaper (per vector) and rerank per-call is higher. Optimize recommends quantization + smaller rerank model for scale workloads. We'll send a tailored pricing sheet.
[04:45] Raj: How does fallback work if capacity is constrained? We can't have the search page fail for users.
[04:52] Priya: We have smart routing and fallbacks — traffic can route to a compatible cheaper model or a regional replica. Also automatic circuit breaker with graceful degradation to recall-only results while queuing rerank.
[05:30] (transcription: "circuit breaker" sometimes shows as "circit breaker")
[06:15] Priya: Let me switch to the Console — here's the embeddings endpoint page, you can pick model, dimension, and set up auto-refresh. Console also surfaces token-cost per call and per-route latency histograms.
[07:02] Priya: Now I'll run a sample query — copying in "wireless earbuds noise cancellation issues" — first we call embeddings recall (KNN) then rerank with a 2-stage prompt.
[07:35] (typing sounds)
[08:02] Priya: First pass recall returned 50 candidates in 35ms, rerank call returned final top 5 in 110ms. You can see tokens and cost on the right panel.
[08:20] Ana: Those numbers look good. What about caching — if users ask follow-up queries we want to reuse KV to avoid recomputing long context.
[08:30] Priya: Exactly — KV cache holds decoder key-value cache for conversation history. For search flows we also do prefix/KV caching for static context to save repeated encoder cost. Note: sometimes transcription shows KV as "K V".
[09:10] Raj: We're also concerned about data privacy and logs retention. What logs do you keep for hosted?
[09:20] Evan: Hosted keeps audit logs, request metadata and optional full transcripts. For customers who want lower retention we can configure minimal logging; SOC 2 controls, SSO (SAML), RBAC, and KMS integrations are available. We'll attach the security pack with encryption/keys details.
[10:05] Mark: Do you support bringing your own KMS?
[10:09] Evan: Yes, BYOK via customer managed keys in supported cloud KMS and HSM integrations for Private; hosted also supports customer-managed keys in some regions. We'll specify in the security doc.
[11:00] Priya: Back to Optimize — the product suggests model quantization, batching recommendations, and cache policies. For example it suggested int8 quantization for the reranker in our tests which cut cost ~2.3x with <1% relevance drop on similar corpora.
[11:45] Ana: Is that validated on our dataset or just general?
[11:50] Priya: Generalized benchmarks. For the pilot we'll run your 1k query set through Optimize and produce per-model regressions — that's part of the pilot scope.
[12:30] (minor crosstalk)
[13:05] Raj: Walk me through the pilot success metrics — what's acceptable?
[13:12] Priya: Typically customers define precision@10 or MRR improvement vs baseline, plus latency SLOs (p95 < 400ms) and cost per 1k queries. For this pilot we suggested target +12% precision@10 and p95 under 450ms.
[14:02] Mark: Our baseline is ~28% precision@10 and p95 600ms. If you can get us to 35-36% with p95 under 450, that's compelling.
[14:20] Evan: Great, that aligns to a 12-15% improvement target. We'll propose exact metrics in the runbook.
[15:00] Priya: Now quick deep dive on reranker design — it's a pointwise vs pairwise architecture; we support both styles depending on latency versus quality tradeoffs. Our hosted reranker endpoint can serve pairwise comparisons in batch to reduce repeated encoding.
[16:05] Ana: Could we run a hybrid where recall is an approximate vector index, then a small embed-based re-scoring before the reranker?
[16:12] Priya: Yes, that's common — approximate recall -> cheap embed-based score -> full neural rerank for top K. Optimize can recommend K and thresholds based on traffic patterns.
[17:00] (transcription: "approximate" sometimes "appoximate")
[18:05] Raj: Any limitations on index size or documents? We have ~8M product descriptions and some image metadata.
[18:15] Priya: For hosted we recommend sharded vector indexes with replication. 8M is fine; we'll discuss shard count during pilot. For very large corpora, Dedicated or Private might be better for predictable throughput but hosted remains a good start.
[19:00] Mark: What about rate limits and burst capacity during sales events?
[19:10] Evan: You can request reserved capacity or Dedicated pools; for hosted we have autoscale with burst buckets but sustained high QPS is better with Dedicated. Pricing reflects reserved capacity commitments.
[20:00] Ana: Can we run A/B tests with two rerank models? We want to validate quality before a full rollout.
[20:06] Priya: Yes — Console supports canary rollouts and A/B tests with automatic metric capture (precision, clicks). You can route percentage traffic and compare.
[21:00] (ambient keyboard)
[22:30] Priya: I'll share a demo script and an example Notebook for how to call embeddings and rerank endpoints programmatically. (link pasted: https://redwood.example/demo-notebook)
[23:10] Raj: Good. On security again: do you do contract-level DPA and data residency?
[23:18] Evan: Yes, DPA included in enterprise contracts; data residency options by region and Private deployments for strict residency. We'll surface the residency matrix in the security pack.
[24:05] Ana: For the pilot, we'd like to limit data retention of raw payloads to 7 days. Is that doable on hosted?
[24:12] Evan: We can propose limited retention; need legal review but technically configurable. We'll note as a requirement in the runbook.
[25:00] Priya: Ok let's run three quick live queries that mimic your internal support search queries. First: "charging case not recognized".
[25:32] (query run)
[26:05] Priya: Recall returned 200 candidates, rerank returned top answer referencing a known firmware bug article (id: 4923). You can see rerank rationale in structured output — we support structured tokens explaining signals.
[26:50] Mark: That rationale snippet is useful for UX to show why we surfaced that doc.
[27:10] Priya: Yes, the API has 'explain' fields, but you can disable for latency-sensitive calls.
[28:00] (brief silence)
[28:15] Ana: A couple of nitty-gritty Qs — how are embeddings stored and versioned? We need reproducibility across model upgrades.
[28:24] Priya: Embedding versions are recorded per vector and you can pin model versions. Console has versioning metadata and snapshot exports for re-indexing when you upgrade embeddings.
[29:05] Raj: Does Console let us compare embeddings quality between two models?
[29:12] Priya: Yes, there's an embedding-eval tab where you can run pairwise MRR checks on test sets. It can also run batch scoring.
[30:00] Mark: Any gotchas we should be aware of for migration from Pinecone?
[30:12] Priya: Data export/import scripts, index mapping differences (some tokenization differences), and sometimes you'd need to re-embed if your previous model differs. We have migration playbooks.
[31:00] (transcription: "tokenization" auto-corrected to "tokinization")
[32:15] Evan: Let's talk pricing bands quickly. For pilots we often give a trial credit or pilot discount. Post-pilot, pricing depends on vector storage, per-embedding cost, rerank call units, and retention tiers. I'll follow up with concrete numbers.
[33:10] Raj: Good. Our procurement also wants SLA details — what uptime SLA do you offer for hosted?
[33:18] Evan: Hosted has a 99.9% uptime target for S0 customers, enterprise SLA available for Dedicated. We'll attach SLA docs.
[34:20] Priya: One more feature note: Optimize can suggest batching window sizes. For interactive web search you might pick small windows (20ms) vs background batch jobs that can tolerate 200ms to get much better throughput.
[35:05] Ana: Are there SDKs for JS and Python? We use Node for frontend server.
[35:10] Evan: Yes official SDKs for JS, Python, and Go. We'll send the JS snippet in the follow-up.
[36:00] (background: toddler noise briefly)
[37:10] Mark: For the pilot we want control plane access for our SREs. How granular is RBAC?
[37:18] Priya: RBAC supports route-level and model-level roles, audit trails, and SSO. We can map your org roles to Console roles.
[38:20] Raj: Hypothetical: if the pilot validates well, what timeline for Dedicated?
[38:26] Evan: If you hit sustained QPS and want reserved capacity, Dedicated provisioning is typically 4-6 weeks from contract, depending on region.
[39:00] Ana: Any performance anti-patterns you see that would hurt latency?
[39:06] Priya: Large batch windows, unbounded document sizes, enabling heavy "explain" payloads on p95 sensitive paths. Also reembedding on every request instead of storing embeddings. We'll highlight best practices in the runbook.
[40:00] (small echo)
[41:10] Evan: Quick recap of next steps: we'll send security pack + SLA + pilot runbook + pricing; Priya will prepare pilot configs; Ana will upload samples. Pilot kickoff scheduled for week of Jan 26.
[41:40] Mark: Sounds good, minor ask — can you include a simple performance spreadsheet that maps p95 to cost per 10k queries under different models?
[41:52] Evan: Yes we'll include that.
[42:10] Raj: Also: include a column for UX impact of enabling explain vs not.
[42:16] Priya: Will do.
[43:00] (wrap-up)
[44:05] Evan: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the docs. If any urgent items, email Evan@redwood.example.
[44:20] Mark: Thanks Evan, Priya. Appreciate it.
[44:30] (call ends, transcription continues capturing faint outro)

Meeting notes end.
